_doc: Combat and casualty tuning (0.5). Every threshold, timer and chance of the health-condition, incapacitation, rescue, hit-feedback and killfeed systems lives here; no code compares health against a literal.

health._doc: Conditions by fraction of maximum health. A character is FINE above caution, CAUTION above injured, INJURED above critical, CRITICAL below. Per condition, in that order: movement speed multiplier, whether sprinting is possible, aim-error multiplier, how quickly locomotion blends respond (1 = normal), strength of the injury animation layer.

maxHealth._doc: Yellow Herbs raise maximum health permanently, to a cap. The upgrade is stored on the profile and survives prestige.

downed._doc: Incapacitation is rare and only for humans. chance: probability that otherwise-lethal damage downs instead of kills, per kind of character. overkill: damage beyond zero health, as a fraction of maximum health, above which the hit is simply fatal. types: multiplier on the chance by how the damage was delivered (0 = always fatal). Fatal regions bypass incapacitation altogether.

revive._doc: A rescuer within range holds on the casualty for time seconds. Taking a hit, moving off or being pinned interrupts it and the casualty is DOWNED again with whatever time was left. Revival restores health to the given fraction of maximum - critical, not healed.

ai._doc: Weights of the rescue decision (brief 5.5). A rescuer goes only when the total is above threshold.

hitmarker._doc: Centre-screen confirmation. life seconds; size in UI pixels at scale 1.

dialogue._doc: Speech bubbles over heads: seconds per line (plus per character), fade distance, wrap width in UI pixels.

decapitation._doc: 0.6. What a killing head shot does to the head, by weapon family. never: this family cannot. Otherwise the chance is (force - chanceFrom) / chanceSpan, capped at max, and only at or above minForce (force = the damage of the killing hit after the head multiplier). closeRange/closeChance: inside this many metres the chance is closeChance outright. Blast always can.

perception._doc: 0.6. How characters see and hear. edgeOfVision: how fast something at the edge of the field of view registers compared with something looked straight at (1 = no difference). verticalDegrees: how steeply above or below itself an unalerted watcher notices things. throughFog: the share of the fog bank's closing distance anyone can see through (nobody sees or shoots from beyond it). throughAFloor: what a floor between leaves of a sound that is not gunfire. alertHearing: how much further the alerted hear.

feeding._doc: 0.6. The infected eat human corpses, which visibly waste away and are finally gone (what the body carried is left on the ground). seconds: how long one infected takes to finish a body alone (several are proportionally quicker); reach: how near it must be to start; seek: how far the walking dead drift toward a body.

fog._doc: 0.6. The fog bank. The world begins to dissolve at start metres and is gone by end (kept inside the 260 m draw distance, so nothing ever pops in). haze multiplies the ordinary near haze; sky is how much of the bank hangs overhead (1 = no sky at all); night and rain bring the bank nearer by these factors. 0.9: 'mist' is how many times thicker the haze is at the mistiest hour (just after first light; the night holds 70% of it, the afternoon none) and 'mistWall' how near the bank then stands (1 = unmoved).

shotgun._doc: 0.6. Shotguns hit harder: damageMul on every pellet, and closeBonus more inside closeRange metres (the charge has not spread).

nametag._doc: 0.6. Names over heads: metres within which a stranger in view is named, the same for the infected, how far a squadmate's name carries (always shown, dimmer through walls), and the text size in UI pixels.

cover._doc: Player contextual cover: how close to an obstacle and how slow before the body settles against it; lean offsets in metres.
